summary: The chapter adheres precisely to the plan and source research. It establishes an operational, workflow-based framework for evaluating supplier quality management software across qualification, receiving inspection, and SCAR integration. Core capabilities are clearly distinguished from pending roadmap items, referencing the capability register status on the ICC product page and auditor guidance from the ISO 9001 APG. Each subsection systematically addresses its assigned role, input, decision, record, exception, and evaluation criteria, supplemented by clearly labeled illustrative examples. Unassigned FAQ content is correctly omitted, and all links match approved sources.

glossary.definition: A comparative evaluation record scoring software capabilities against operational workflow requirements, noting whether features are verified with sample data, unverified, or pending release.
An unalterable, automated log of user actions, status modifications, inspection dispositions, and evidence attachment updates that records timestamps and user identities.

recordNames: Vendor evaluation matrix with capability validation statuses and architectural risk notes
Controlled nonconformance disposition record with author identity, review timestamp, and electronic signature
Security and access control validation protocol detailing permission test outcomes
Total cost of ownership evaluation sheet detailing implementation, licensing, and validation costs
decisions: Determine which software vendors meet mandatory operational integration criteria for formal demonstration
Accept, modify, or reject AI-generated nonconformance descriptions and disposition recommendations
Determine if system audit trail meets electronic signature integrity and data tampering prevention standards
Determine whether licensing models align with operational headcount across receiving bays and quality teams
